facts.fact: The International Growth Centre's study of the four city councils, researched to early 2022, reports the revenue system vendors saying the cities chose cloud-based systems and so had to secure enough internet bandwidth at their local government offices, that some had to upgrade their connectivity when the systems were rolled out, and that Blantyre took seven months to install bandwidth sufficient for its system.
facts.system: City councils' office internet for cloud-based Revenue Management Systems

facts.fact: The International Growth Centre's study says staff of the Blantyre, Lilongwe, Mzuzu and Zomba city councils work in cloud-based Revenue Management Systems introduced from 2017, generating, authorising and printing demand notices and business licences online and watching market point-of-sale devices in real time, with depth varying by city and Lilongwe's use described as low; none had been integrated with the local IFMIS or the banks by the time of the research in early 2022.
facts.system: Revenue Management Systems of the four city councils

facts.fact: The International Growth Centre's study describes cloud-based revenue systems, and the office internet they need, at four local governments, the city councils of Blantyre, Lilongwe, Mzuzu and Zomba, of the 35 local governments it counts (28 district, 4 city and 3 municipal councils); it studied only the four and says nothing of the connection of the other 31.
facts.system: Revenue Management Systems of the four city councils

facts.fact: The International Growth Centre's study, dated August 2023, finds the four city councils have no comprehensive IT strategy and bring in systems piecemeal without working out what they need in infrastructure such as local internet connectivity, and that there was no national push or coordination behind the systems.
facts.system: City councils' office internet for cloud-based Revenue Management Systems

facts.fact: The International Growth Centre's study reports that securing internet bandwidth at council offices, and connectivity for market point-of-sale devices (usually a mobile SIM card), was the responsibility of the city councils themselves and not of the software vendors, who run the revenue systems for 3 to 20 per cent of the revenue handled; the owner of the connection is the local authority, not a ministry.
facts.system: City councils' office internet for cloud-based Revenue Management Systems

systems.system: Blantyre City Council Revenue Management System
systems.platform: TechnoBrain; build-operate-transfer for 15-20% of revenue over seven years; 60 point-of-sale devices for 200 ticket sellers
systems.tiers: city rates, business licences and market rates from 2020-2021; the agreement put on hold after figures did not tally with the city's accounts

systems.system: Lilongwe City Council Revenue Management System
systems.platform: Nitel; software licence for 20% of revenue over five years; cloud storage; 40 point-of-sale devices for 90 ticket sellers
systems.tiers: city rates, business licences and market rates from 2019-2020; use described as low

systems.system: Mzuzu City Council REMOP and automated revenue management system
systems.platform: REMOP, donor-provided, 2013, for city rates; ARMS by TechnoBrain for 15% of revenue, with 90 point-of-sale devices, in use from December 2021
systems.owner: Mzuzu City Council; donors; vendor TechnoBrain

systems.system: Zomba City Council Revenue Management System
systems.platform: Nitel; software licence for 3% of revenue; about 15 point-of-sale devices in 2017, 40 for 50 or more ticket sellers later
systems.tiers: market rates, bus depots and parking from 2017; point-of-sale devices out of use from 2019 and only a handful back by early 2022

rolled out to the 36 local governments from 2009, rural councils first; city councils from 2015; no interface with the national IFMIS, receipts uploaded by hand; a new national IFMIS not yet at local level
named as the network the national IFMIS's 50 servers had to be joined to in the early 2000s; no council office said to be on it

note: Read whole. The `owner:ministry` fact is forced by the closed list: the document makes the city council itself, a local authority, responsible for its own internet, and the parent should read it as 'the state, local'. The four are the country's cities, the capital among them; the study is silent on district and municipal councils. Point-of-sale devices on SIM cards in markets are not the office's connection and give no fact.
